A1.justification: Both complete, readable 17-page PDFs describe ReflexSplit. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material can be matched reliably, including the renumbered architecture table.

before.justification: v1 reports original reflection-separation experiments, cross-dataset evaluations, component ablations and feature analyses in Tables 1–6 and associated figures.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds computational-efficiency results in Table 7.

M1.justification: The dual-branch architecture, CrGF, LFSB, curriculum schedule, losses and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The architecture table is renumbered from Table 7 to Table 8 without substantive changes.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same PASCAL VOC-derived data, real training pairs, Nature, Real20, SIR2 subsets and OpenRR-1K coverage. The efficiency comparison introduces no new dataset, domain or reflection-separation scenario.

E2.justification: New Table 7 compares efficiency against DExNet, MaxRF, DSIT, RDNet and DAI. DAI was previously cited in related work but lacked reported quantitative comparison. Comparator membership in the existing accuracy experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds an efficiency evaluation at 384 × 384 input resolution, reporting FLOPs, inference time and FPS. Existing accuracy metrics, dataset splits, preprocessing and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 13 and Table 7 add a focused analysis of computational cost alongside training-stage complexity and reflection-separation capability. Existing component ablations, t-SNE/PCA analyses, performance-margin analysis and failure cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the experimental comparisons. The new efficiency measurements also appear as point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds efficiency results, including ReflexSplit's 969.050 GFLOPs, 211.349 ms and 4.73 FPS, versus RDNet's 1047.141 GFLOPs, 122.800 ms and 8.14 FPS. Existing accuracy scores and qualitative findings are retained; no same-setting accuracy improvement is reported.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, equations and algorithmic specification are retained. The new efficiency section introduces no theoretical assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims concerning explicit fusion-separation, cross-scale coordination, curriculum training, perceptual quality and generalization.

C2.justification: New Section 13 interprets the efficiency results as a favorable balance between computational cost, single-stage training and reflection-output capability, and asserts deployment suitability. It acknowledges MaxRF's speed advantage while distinguishing its output capability. Existing failure-condition discussions are unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 7 newly documents single- versus multiple-stage training and reflection-output support across the compared methods. Existing optimizer settings, hyperparameters, hardware statement, architecture details and code-access information remain unchanged; no implementation modification is established.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work section are unchanged. Section 13 adds practical positioning relative to those methods, emphasizing ReflexSplit's single-stage separation capability against multistage methods and faster methods without direct reflection output.

P1.justification: v2 adds the supplementary 'More Complexity Comparison' section and its overview entry. The author name 'Jing-Hui Jung' becomes 'Jin-Hui Jiang'. Otherwise, the existing prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the efficiency table as Table 7 and renumbers the architecture table to Table 8. Supplementary text and references reflow around the additions. Existing figures and their visual content are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 discussed efficiency mainly through parameter counts; v2 adds useful computational-cost, latency and capability evidence. Table 7 makes tradeoffs clearer, including slower reported inference than RDNet despite fewer parameters. This improves transparency modestly, although detailed timing procedures remain unspecified and the deployment claim receives limited direct support. The central method and accuracy evidence are unchanged.
